claim: The average most expensive West End ticket rose 5.2% to £162.61 in 2026, while the average cheapest ticket is £30.55, up over 24% from 2024.
quote: The average most expensive West End ticket is up 5.2%, from £154.56 in 2024 to £162.61 in 2026. However, the average cheapest ticket for a show in London is £30.55, up by over 24% from 2024, when the average lowest price was £24.58.

claim: Most West End tickets sell for £56 or less, a quarter cost under £35, and fewer than 4% exceed £150; the priciest single seat in 2026 was Moulin Rouge! at £303.83.
quote: Most West End tickets were purchased at £56 or less, and a quarter cost under £35, while fewer than four per cent of tickets exceeded £150... Moulin Rouge! ... certain seats costing £303.83

claim: Balcony seats typically range £10-£40, stalls and dress circle £50-£100, and premium seats £100-£200+, with most West End shows using airline-style dynamic pricing that rises with demand.
quote: Balcony seats can range from £10 to £40, stalls and dress circle seats vary from £50 to £100, and premium seats for highly sought-after productions range from £100-£200+. ... prices fluctuate based on demand, day of week, time of year

claim: TodayTix releases same-day app-exclusive Rush tickets at 10am daily on a first-come basis and runs daily randomly-drawn Lottery entries for top West End shows, at a fraction of box-office price.
quote: Most London shows release Rush at 10 AM local time the day of the performance ... Rush and Lottery tickets are typically a fraction of the box office price

claim: Day seats/rush tickets are typically £20-£30 released ~10am at box offices, lotteries often £20-25, and TKTS offers 20-50% discounts; cheapest booking is Tuesday-Thursday and in January-February.
quote: often between £20 and £30 ... ticket lotteries ... often £20-25 ... TKTS Booth ... discounts of 20-50% ... January and February are the cheapest months

claim: The TKTS booth in Leicester Square's Clocktower building is the only ticket booth run by the not-for-profit Society of London Theatre; other shops in the square are not official, and online inventory refreshes daily at 12:01am.
quote: run by the Society of London Theatre, a not-for-profit organisation ... There are other ticket shops in the square but we are the only one run by the Society of London Theatre ... new inventory released daily at 12:01am

claim: Viagogo resale carries 25-30% fees and inflated prices, and the same tickets are almost always cheaper elsewhere, so check the official box office first.
quote: fees reaching 25-30%, inflated prices ... The same tickets are almost always available cheaper on other platforms, especially if you check the official box office first.

claim: Paris's Kiosque Culture booth next to the Madeleine church (15 place de la Madeleine) sells same-day half-price tickets to around 150 shows, open Tue-Sat with no phone pre-booking.
quote: The Kiosque Culture next to the Madeleine church offers around 150 shows ... half-price same-day theater tickets ... open Tuesday to Saturday, 12:30 to 2:30 pm and 3 pm to 7:30 pm ... you have to go to the kiosk

claim: In Paris, tickets can be booked via online offices such as Ticketac, Fnac Spectacles, or directly on theatre websites.
quote: You can book your tickets through online ticket offices such as Ticketac, Fnac Spectacles or directly on the theatres' websites.

claim: Vienna's big musicals (Raimund Theater, Ronacher) are produced by Vereinigte Bühnen Wien and booked officially at musicalvienna.at, with Vienna PASS holders getting 20% off categories A-D.
quote: VBW productions can be booked online at www.musicalvienna.at ... Vienna PASS customers receive a 20% discount on current VBW productions for up to 4 tickets in categories A-D
